rv.q: It's a gripping, socio-political railroad powered by Pike's breathless performance.
It's a roller coaster of a show for which Pike may well win an Olivier Award this coming Sunday.
Pike is in constant motion, slipping in and out of outfits, catching a casually flung lemon, and keeping up a sometimes amused, sometimes emotionally frayed commentary.
But for all the quality of the production, I have the nagging feeling that deep down it's really a lecture.
It's familiar material, but Pike's humour and commitment and the confidence of the production elevate it.
It is slick (perhaps too much so) and entertaining, but also has the courage of its convictions in the questions it raises.
Pike masterfully works her way through Miller
But Miller is very good at exploring the ambiguity of rape cases.
The play breathlessly unpicks its knotty moral conundrum, packaged in a style that grates.
Pike is an inherently physical performer, and flaws in the script are glossed over by her constant bounding around the set
Pike's solo performance is utterly breathless while she commands the space as a maverick judge.
Inter Alia is a must-watch for everyone who has produced or has ever been a child.
Pike is an absolute force. Authentic in her role, she is entirely convincing as Judge and mother.
Believe the hype. Inter Alia will have you feeling every emotion possible and you'll think about it for days.
It's a blistering time to examine masculinity and Miller is leading the charge.
Pike powers through the evening in what is surely one of the best performances of the year.
Despite a few imperfections, Inter Alia is an exhilarating and relevant examination of law and morality, feminism and motherhood, and gender politics.
